title: Teacher Workflow No. 04: the book half your students never bought
author: Doan Winkel
summary: Doan Winkel's How to Teach With AI series offers a five-step workflow for replacing most of an expensive assigned textbook with free, verified material and a course reader. The premise is that many students go weeks without the book and instructors rarely use more than a third of it, yet the easy path at adoption time is to click same as last term. In steps one to three the instructor uses a chat tool to map what job each chapter does, to find open-licensed candidates for each job, and then opens every link personally because chat tools invent sources with total confidence. Step four loads the surviving sources into NotebookLM and makes it report coverage and gaps with citations, and step five generates unit reading guides that the instructor reviews before posting. A fifteen-minute version and a one-chapter version are offered for busy instructors, and the whole build takes about three hours once.
points: The workflow starts by naming the job each chapter does in the course, so that chapters with no clear job are the first to be replaced.
Every AI-suggested source must be opened and checked for existence, open license and fit, because a candidate the instructor has not opened should be treated as nonexistent.
NotebookLM is used to check its own coverage against the job table, with the instructor spot-checking citations before trusting the reader.
Reading guides generated from the reader give students a unit-by-unit path with cited questions, and the instructor deletes any question they would not ask in class.
A smaller version, swapping only the one chapter you already skip half of, keeps the effort realistic before the adoption deadline.
quotes: The bookstore wants your spring adoptions, and on most campuses the easiest thing to do is click “same as last term.
This workflow finds that third and swaps the rest for free material you’ve checked yourself. Students get a course reader that answers their questions with citations.
Any chapter where you cannot write that line is the first one to replace.
Chat tools can invent sources with total confidence, including real-looking links to books that don’t exist.
Anything that fails one check comes off the list. A candidate you have not opened does not exist.
Replacing half the book with material you trust beats replacing all of it with material you guessed at.
Don’t replace the whole book. Run steps 1 through 3 on the one chapter you already skip half of, and swap that chapter alone.
